sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Faraday’s First Law**: An **EMF** is induced in a circuit whenever the **magnetic flux** linked with it changes.
• **Faraday’s Second Law**: The magnitude of the induced EMF is directly proportional to the **rate of change of magnetic flux**.
• **Lenz’s Law**: The direction of the induced current is such that it **opposes the change** in magnetic flux that produced it (Conservation of Energy).
• **Key Metric**: **Magnetic Flux (Φ)** = B · A · cos(θ), where B is magnetic field, A is area, and θ is the angle between the field and the normal to the surface.

items.definition: Circular loops of current induced in bulk conductors by changing magnetic fields; cause heating (Joule heating) and energy loss.
A device based on mutual induction that changes AC voltage levels; does not work on DC because DC produces constant flux.

items.title: Major Applications
items.content:
• **Electric Generators**: Convert mechanical energy to electrical energy via rotation in a magnetic field.
• **Induction Cooktops**: Use high-frequency magnetic fields to induce eddy currents directly in the cookware base.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Energy Loss**: Hysteresis and eddy current losses in transformers.
• **Solutions**: Use of laminated cores and soft iron materials to minimize heat dissipation.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'FLR' (Fleming's Left/Right).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Right hand for Generators (Right-hand rule for induced current); Left hand for Motors (Left-hand rule for force).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often tests if transformers work on DC. Remember: Transformers require changing flux, hence they ONLY work on AC.
Mains Value Addition: Link 'Eddy Currents' to 'Magnetic Braking' in high-speed trains (Maglev) as a sustainable transport solution.

keyTakeaways: Lenz's Law is a direct consequence of the Law of Conservation of Energy.
Transformers are strictly AC devices; they cannot step up or step down DC voltage.
Eddy currents are generally undesirable in transformers but useful in induction heating and braking systems.
